question.text: A club deal is being formed by three Cat II AIFs to take 'Bharat Consumer Products Ltd.' private via a delisting offer. The target is a listed, cash-generative, under-leveraged mid-cap. Which buy-out archetype is MOST likely to be structured here?

answer.text: Management Buy-In (MBI) with totally new external team
Venture Capital Series-A round with founder top-up
Pure growth-capital PE round with minority stake
Leveraged Buy-Out (LBO) where significant acquisition debt is raised against target cashflows

explanation.text: The Logic: An LBO is used where a target has attractive cash flows and low existing leverage, allowing significant acquisition leverage to be raised against those cash flows. The classic structure is approximately 70% debt and 30% equity. The target described — listed, cash-generative, under-leveraged — fits the LBO template. The Trap: Option A (MBI) requires an external management team to lead the buyout, which the fact pattern does not describe. Option B confuses Series-A early-stage venture financing with a control buyout. Option C contradicts the delisting/control objective. Note: Look for two LBO-tell-tale features in the stem: stable free cash flows and a lightly geared balance sheet.
